articles.title: NRLA ramps up campaign against rent controls
articles.summary: Concern is growing that the new PM wants private sector rent controls
articles.ai_summary:
- The National Residential Landlords Association (NRLA) intensifies efforts to oppose potential rent controls in the private sector amid rising concerns regarding the new Prime Minister's stance.
- Landlords are alarmed as speculation mounts that the government may implement measures limiting rental prices.

articles.title: Tenants know rent controls push out landlords – but still want them
articles.summary: It's a survey of 5,607 tenants by flat-sharing website SpareRoom
articles.ai_summary:
- A SpareRoom survey reveals that despite acknowledging that rent controls may drive landlords away, a majority of 5,607 tenants still support implementing them.  
- Tenants express a strong desire for rent stability, even as they recognize potential negative impacts on housing supply from such regulations.

articles.title: Huge expansion of licensing planned for another London council
articles.summary: A council currently has selective licensing across five wards but wants to expand
articles.ai_summary:
- A London council plans a substantial expansion of its selective licensing program, currently active in five wards.  
- The proposed changes aim to enhance oversight and improve housing standards across more areas of the borough.

articles.title: Landlords urged to report hate crimes on behalf of tenants
articles.summary: It's a “mad” policy according to a leading political magazine.
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords are being encouraged to report hate crimes on behalf of tenants, sparking controversy in the UK property sector.  
- Critics label the initiative as "mad," highlighting concerns over its practicality and implications for landlord-tenant relations.

articles.title: Massive growth of landlord companies still accelerating
articles.summary: Nearly 14,000 registered in the first five months of 2026
articles.ai_summary:
- Over 13,800 new landlord companies registered in the UK within just the first five months of 2026.  
- The rapid increase reflects a continuing surge in the property rental market.

articles.title: Burnham has “genuine interest in property standards” says NRLA chief
articles.summary: The NRLA chief executive has written to he new PM outlining a vision for private renting
articles.ai_summary:
- NRLA chief executive highlights Burnham's commitment to improving property standards in the private rental sector.
- A letter to the new Prime Minister outlines a forward-thinking vision for enhancing private renting in the UK.

articles.title: Burnham lobbied to test private rent controls in one city
articles.summary: Labour wants mayors to get powers to improve rent control regimes
articles.ai_summary:
- Labour is advocating for mayors to gain the authority to implement and test private rent control measures in Burnham and other cities.  
- The initiative aims to enhance housing affordability and tenant protections amid rising rental costs.

articles.title: Rayner’s Back! Burnham’s surprise choice as Housing Secretary
articles.summary: Rayner resigned from the post 10 months ago - and now she's back
articles.ai_summary:
- Angela Rayner makes a surprising return as Housing Secretary just 10 months after her resignation.  
- Her comeback signals a shift in Burnham's leadership strategy amidst ongoing housing challenges in the UK.

articles.title: Labour bid to clampdown on Airbnbs and other short lets
articles.summary: A Private Member’s Bill wants a reduction in the freedom of short let landlords.
articles.ai_summary:
- The Labour Party is proposing a Private Member's Bill aimed at restricting the rights of short let landlords, including those operating on platforms like Airbnb.  
- The initiative seeks to regulate short-term rentals to address housing concerns and increase available long-term rental options.

articles.title: Landlords resort to auctions to shift units as Renters Rights Act kicks in
articles.summary: Activity is up by over a third
articles.ai_summary:
- Landlords are increasingly turning to auctions to sell properties as the new Renters Rights Act takes effect.  
- Auction activity has surged by over 30%, reflecting a proactive response to upcoming regulatory changes.

articles.title: Renters’ chief quits, taking part-credit for Section 21 abolition
articles.summary: Ben Twomey joined Generation Rent in a role upgraded from director to chief executive
articles.ai_summary:
- Ben Twomey steps down as CEO of Generation Rent, having played a significant role in advocating for the abolition of Section 21 evictions.  
- His departure comes amid ongoing debates about renters' rights and housing policies in the UK.

articles.title: Council threat to pursue convicted landlords over damp and mould
articles.summary: The landlords ignored an Improvement Notice

articles.title: Landlords and tenants poles apart on rent levels, says top agency
articles.summary: The analysis is of prime rental markets across the UK
